questions.question: ​_________ accounts for the difference between the concept of market price and factor cost in national income measurement.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net indirect taxes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **difference between market price and factor cost in national income measurement is accounted for by net indirect taxes, **which is the difference between indirect taxes and subsidies
 
• **Market price includes the impact of indirect taxe**s, but not subsidies.
 
• **Factor cost only considers the actual cost of production, including profit**, and may not reflect the effect of taxes and subsidies. 
 
• The national product **can be measured at either market prices or factor cost, and the difference between the two is the amount of net indirect taxes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indirect taxes**

 
 
• Taxes **levied on the production, sale, purchase, or use of goods and services**.
 
• Examples i**nclude excise duties, sales tax, value added tax, import and export duties,** and entertainment tax.
 
• Indirect taxes increase the price paid in a transaction compared to the actual receipts of the factor of production. 
 
 
 
• **Subsidies**
 
 
• Government expenditures f**or individuals, households, and businesses to stabilize the econom**y.
 
• Subsidies are the difference between the market price and the cost of production. 
 
 
 
• **Direct taxes**
 
 
• **Taxes levied directly on income,** such as personal income tax and corporate tax.

questions.question:
Consider the following factors.

a) Extreme climatic conditions in the Himalayas and the Indian Thar Desert.

b) Lack of medical facilities in rural areas.

c) Availability of employment in metro cities.

d) Poverty in rural India.

e) Education facilities in urban areas.

Which of the given factors are NOT pull factor(s) for migration in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only a,b and d**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **a) Extreme climatic conditions in the Himalayas and the Indian Thar Desert**

 
 
• These are** difficult and often life-threatening conditions** that force people to migrate elsewhere for better living environments.
 
• **Example:** Harsh winters in the Himalayas or arid conditions in the Thar Desert push people toward more hospitable areas.
 
• This is a** push factor, not a pull facto**r.
 
 
 
• **b) Lack of medical facilities in rural areas**
 
 
• **Poor access to healthcare in rural areas forces people to migrate to urban areas** with better medical infrastructure.
 
• **Example:** People moving from villages to cities for hospitals and specialized treatments.
 
• This is a** push factor, not a pull factor.**
 
 
 
• **c) Availability of employment in metro cities**
 
 
• Cities often o**ffer better job opportunities, higher wages, and diverse industries, attracting people from rural or less developed areas.**
 
• Migrants moving to Mumbai or Delhi for work in factories, offices, or construction.
 
• This is a **pull factor as it draws people to the **cities.
 
 
 
• **d) Poverty in rural India**
 
 
• Poverty **compels people to leave rural areas in search of better living conditions**.
 
• It is a negative factor at the place of origin.
 
• **Example: **Farmers or laborers moving to urban areas to escape poverty and earn a livelihood.
 
• **This is a push factor, not a pull factor**.
 
 
 
• **e) Education facilities in urban areas**
 
 
• Cities** often have better schools, colleges, and universities, attracting students and families from rural a**reas.
 
• **Example: **Families migrating to cities like Bengaluru or Chennai for higher education opportunities.
 
• **This is a pull factor, as it attracts people to urban areas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Migration in India is influenced by **push** and **pull factors**:
 
• **Push factors** are negative conditions in the place of origin that force people to leave, such as poverty, lack of facilities, or harsh living conditions.
 
• **Pull factors** are positive conditions or opportunities in the destination that attract people, such as better employment, education, or healthcare.

questions.question: The ‘Make in India’ programme, which started in 2014, is similar to _____________ of the 1970s and 1980s in India.

questions.question: Junagadh Rock Inscription belongs to whom among the following rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudradaman I**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rudradaman I, the greatest of the Saka ruler in India is known to us from his coins, but more so from his Junagarh Inscription dated in the Saka year 72 i.e 150 AD.
 
• It is located on a rock near Girnar hill, in Junagadh, Gujarat.
 
• This i**nscription written in Brahmi scrip**t, entirely in prose, using Sanskrit language was the earliest record ever written in perfect Sanskrit.
 
• The Rudradaman inscription is in fact **one of the three significant inscriptions found on the same rock, dated to be the second in chronology. **
 
• **T**he oldest inscription is a version of Ashoka edicts, while the last and third inscription is of the Gupta Emperor Skandagupta.
 
• The Rudradaman inscription is near the top, above the Ashoka edict.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c59d2477d2f052eec281904289bdf4d8bdc906eb7173b844f176f8a1f8f31d64.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rudradaman I belonged to the Western Kshatrapa dynasty of Kardamkas.
 
• The Western Satraps or Western Kshatrapas (35–405 AD) were Indo-Scythian (Saka) rulers of the western and central parts of India.
 
• Rudradaman took up the title of Maha-Kshtrapa ("Great Satrap") after he became the king and then strengthened his kingdom.

questions.question: Which of the following taxes was related to the land revenue (tax on agricultural land) system of the Delhi sultanate?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Kharaj was a tax on agricultural land under the Delhi sultanate, and its range was one-third to half of the produce.**
 
• Kharaj is mainly** imposed on non-Muslims** and converts them to Islam in recently conquered territories of Islam.
 
• Under the law of Islam, **only native Muslims or those who converted **to Islam were allowed to own land.
 
• Thus, the **non-Muslim cultivators were encouraged to adopt Islam, **so that they could sustain their agricultural holdings.

__
 
• There are different types of tax imposed during the **Delhi sultanate:**

 
 
• **Kharaj **was a land tax that was equal to** one-tenth of the produce of the land.**
 
• **Zakat** was a tax on property realized by the Muslims.
 
• **Kham **was one-fifth of the booty captured, a tax on mines, treasure troves, and a share on war booty.
 
• **Jaziya:** levied on the non-Muslim subjects, particularly the Hindus. Women and children were, however, exempted from the taxes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Mamluk Dynasty/ Slave Dynasty (1206-1290).
 
• The Khilji Dynasty (1290-1320).
 
• The Tughlaq Dynasty (1320-1414).
 
• The Sayyid Dynasty (1414-1451).
 
• The Lodhi Dynasty (1451-1526).
 
 
 
• **Illtutmish was known as the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate.**

• **The quorum for a joint sitting of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha of the Indian Parliament is one-tenth (which is 10%) of the total numbe**r of members in both house

• To break this deadlock, the President calls the joint sitting.
 
• It happens in the case when one house has passed the bill and the other one has rejected, both the houses cannot come on a common page on the amendments to be made to the bill or more than six months time has been elapsed since the bill has been received by the other house and is still not passed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a push factor of globalisation of business?

options.text: Availability of cheap raw material in the host country
Higher rates of return in host economies
Availability of cheap labour in the host country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Saturation of domestic market **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **saturated domestic market** occurs when a country’s market has limited room for growth due to factors like intense competition or a limited number of consumers.
 
• This **creates a push factor for businesses to expand globally in search of new markets and opportunities.**
 
• In a saturated market,** intense competition can result in price wars, reduced profit margins, and difficulty in differentiating products or services.**
 
• **To overcome these challenges, businesses look for opportunities in other markets where they can gain a competitive advantage**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other Factors are
 
• **Shift in Consumer Preferences**:
 
 
• Changes in consumer preferences or the emergence of new trends may lead to a decline in demand for certain products or services.
 
• Businesses often push for expansion into new markets to adapt to these shifts and diversify their offerings.
 
 
 
• **Economic Cycles and Business Lifecycle**:
 
 
• During economic downturns or in the later stages of a business lifecycle, growth opportunities in the domestic market may become limited.
 
• This pushes businesses to explore international markets for sustained growth.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements and Globalization**:
 
 
• As technology continues to evolve and global markets become more interconnected, businesses may see global expansion as a way to leverage innovation and stay competitive.

questions.question: Which one of the following articles of the Constitution of India deals with the limitations of the executive powers of the State?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Article 162** of the Constitution of India defines the extent of the executive power of the State.
 
• It states that the executive power of a State shall extend to the matters with respect to which the Legislature of the State has power to make laws.
 
• However, the executive power of a State is subject to and limited by the executive power expressly conferred by the Constitution or by any law made by the Parliament.
 
• This article ensures that the executive actions of the State do not overstep the boundaries set by the Constitution and the laws enacted by the Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 168**

 
 
• Article 168 of the Indian Constitution deals with the **composition of state legislatures.**
 
• It states that every State shall have a Legislature which shall consist of the Governor and one House or two Houses, as the case may be.
 
 
 
• **Article 177**
 
 
• Article 177 deals with the **rights of Ministers and Advocate-General** as respects the **Houses of Legislatures**.
 
• It states that every Minister and the Advocate-General for a State shall have the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, the Legislative Assembly of the State, and for both Houses in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, but shall not be entitled to vote.
 
 
 
• **Article 165**
 
 
• Article 165 deals with the** Advocate-General for the State**.
 
• It states that the Governor of each State shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of a High Court to be Advocate-General for the State.
